Hi Claire — thanks for the sample and the certificate. A few notes from Redwood AP/tax perspective: 

1) Invoice name normalization
- For automated matching we prefer the VAT ID (field) as the stable key. The vendor legal name can include diacritics (TekFórge) but please also include a plain ASCII version on the invoice header in parentheses, e.g. "TekFórge Ltd (TekForge Ltd)". That avoids OCR mismatches.

2) VAT/Tax ID placement
- Put your UK VAT number in the "Tax ID / VAT ID" line and also in the invoice meta (bottom-left). We also accept it in the invoice number metadata if your system supports custom fields.

3) PO splitting
- If a single invoice should be split across Redwood entities, include a short line item table at the bottom indicating the split percentage and the target PO numbers. Example: 
  - PO: RED-EMEA-12345 (60%)
  - PO: RED-US-9876 (40%)
- Our default is to route by the PO number to the mapped legal entity; without explicit split lines AP will route the full invoice to the entity on the PO.

I've looped in Ben from Tax to confirm the VAT implications of the accented name (Ben — can you confirm whether we need any further evidence for non-standard characters on UK invoices?).

Thanks — I can update our supplier template once we agree.

Lukas Meyer
Procurement Manager | Redwood Inference

Claire / Lukas — quick tax check from my side: 

- The presence of diacritics in the vendor legal name is not a VAT disqualifier for the UK. The crucial element is the VAT registration number and whether the invoice contains the required VAT elements (seller/buyer, invoice date, invoice number, VAT rate, VAT amount, net amount).
- For automated reconciliation we prefer the VAT ID as the unique key; if Companies House lists the name with the accent that's fine as long as the VAT certificate matches. Keep the alternate ASCII name line — that will reduce OCR noise.
- On PO splitting: ensure the invoice references the exact PO numbers and the split amounts. AP will only split if those PO numbers exist on our side and are mapped to the respective billing entities.

Laura — can you confirm the target entity mapping for PO RED-EMEA-12345 vs RED-EMEA-12346 (TekForge will use a single invoice covering both)? We should decide whether AP should route by line item mapping or by explicit split lines on the invoice.

Ben Carter
Sr. Tax Manager, Redwood Inference

Thanks all — decision below so we can close onboarding: 

- Entity mapping: RED-EMEA-12345 -> Redwood EMEA Holdings Ltd (billing entity 1002)
- RED-EMEA-12346 -> Redwood UK Services Ltd (billing entity 1003)

Operational guidance for TekForge: 
- TekForge should provide explicit split lines when a single invoice covers both POs. Format: a short table at the bottom showing PO / entity code / net amount / VAT amount. Example rows: 
  PO | Entity code | Net | VAT
  RED-EMEA-12345 | 1002 | 6,000.00 | 1,200.00
  RED-EMEA-12346 | 1003 | 4,000.00 | 800.00

- If TekForge cannot include split lines, AP will allocate the invoice to the PO displayed in the invoice header (so please include both PO numbers and indicate "Primary PO" for the default).
